title: Potential Impact from Rising Tuition Expenditure on Educational Equity
what_it_is: Potential Impact from Rising Tuition Expenditure on Educational Equity

sections.label: Tuition expenditure and household income
sections.summary: DOS Household Expenditure Survey 2023 found tuition expenditure growth across all households was similar to growth in overall household income.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Based on findings from the Household Expenditure Survey 2023 conducted by the Department of Statistics (DOS), the overall growth in tuition expenditure across all households was similar to the growth in overall household income from all sources.

sections.label: Tuition spending income quintile disparity
sections.summary: DOS data shows a disparity in tuition expenditure between households of different income quintiles, as two Members highlighted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: As Dr Wan Rizal and Mr Yip Hon Weng highlighted, the data from DOS also shows a disparity in tuition expenditure between households of different income quintiles.

sections.label: Collaborative Tuition Programme subsidised tuition
sections.summary: The Collaborative Tuition Programme provides students, particularly those from lower-income households, with subsidised tuition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: One example is the Collaborative Tuition Programme, which provides students, particularly those from lower-income households, with subsidised tuition.

sections.label: Lower socio-economic students post-secondary progress
sections.summary: Nine in 10 students from lower socio-economic status backgrounds progress to post-secondary education today, compared to five in 10 two decades earlier.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Nonetheless, in some areas, the gaps have narrowed over time – for instance, among students from lower socio-economic status backgrounds, nine in 10 students progress to post-secondary education today, compared to five in 10 around two decades earlier.

sections.label: Tuition centre advertising outside schools
sections.summary: A Member asked whether MOE would issue standing instructions advising tuition centres against sales outside schools, especially on Primary 1 first day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Can I ask the Minister of State whether there are any standing instructions or would MOE come out with some standing instructions to advise tuition centres not to do such tuition sales outside schools, especially on the first day of school for Primary 1 students?

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We have observed some tuition centres employing undesirable advertising practices that appeal to parents' anxieties and fear of missing out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Our schools certainly do not support such practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We are studying how we could discourage tuition centres from doing this.

sections.label: School support for weaker students
sections.summary: Teachers raise weaker children's literacy or numeracy needs with parents, and specialised intervention programmes like Reading Remediation and Learning Support for Mathematics support primary students.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: That is why in our schools, if we identify that certain children seem to be weaker and falling behind in basic literacy or numeracy skills, teachers, out of care and concern, will want to bring this to the awareness of parents and work together with them to support the learning of our students.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We understand that, sometimes, some households may not have the resources or abilities, and that is why we have specialised academic intervention programmes for primary school students who need more support in foundational skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: These programmes include the Reading Remediation Programme and Learning Support for Mathematics, and we have seen good outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: More importantly, in building confidence of our students especially those from lower-income households when they go through these programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: These programmes typically have fewer students and special additional resources, and they are done with consent from and also in partnership with the parents.
